sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: To show a ball rolling very fast in a drawing for 'Objects on the Move', what should you add?
options: C) Speed lines or action lines behind it
D) Small dots inside the ball
questions.answer: C) Speed lines or action lines behind it

questions.question_text: When drawing a scene for 'Peeping Out of the Window', the window frame acts as a what?
options: A) A natural border or frame for your view
B) The main subject of the artwork
C) A background element to ignore
questions.answer: A) A natural border or frame for your view

questions.question_text: In 'Picturing Stories', what do we call a series of drawings arranged in boxes to tell a narrative?
options: B) A comic strip or storyboard
questions.answer: B) A comic strip or storyboard

questions.question_text: Which of these is the best example of an 'Imaginary Being' in visual arts?
options: C) A dragon with butterfly wings
questions.answer: C) A dragon with butterfly wings

questions.question_text: Which visual art form is most commonly used for 'Spreading the Message' to a large crowd quickly?
What main materials are required when you 'Stitch it for a Story'?
To 'Create a Scene' that looks deep, how should objects far away be drawn?
options: A) Smaller and higher up on the page
B) Larger and at the very bottom
C) The exact same size as close objects
questions.answer: A) Smaller and higher up on the page

questions.question_text: The 'Time Team Technique' in art refers to what kind of activity?
options: A) Drawing as fast as you can alone
B) Working together collaboratively as a group to create art
questions.answer: B) Working together collaboratively as a group to create art

questions.question_text: What is the primary goal of the 'View and Review' process in an art classroom?
options: A) To hide artwork from others
B) To throw away old sketches
C) To observe artworks closely and share constructive feedback
D) To copy another student's drawing perfectly
questions.answer: C) To observe artworks closely and share constructive feedback

questions.question_text: Which combination represents the primary colors in visual arts used to mix other colors?
How can you use 'action lines' to show that a drawn character is running very fast? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I can draw horizontal trailing lines behind the character's feet and lean their body forward to give a strong feeling of fast forward movement.

questions.question_text: Describe what you might see if you draw a scene titled 'Peeping Out of the Window' on a rainy afternoon. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I would draw raindrops splashing on the glass pane, dark grey clouds in the sky, and people outside holding colorful umbrellas to stay dry.

questions.question_text: Why do artists use posters when 'Spreading the Message' about saving the environment? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Posters use bold colors, large text, and striking images to quickly catch people's attention and effectively communicate the important message of conservation.

questions.question_text: Explain how to create texture in an artwork using the 'Stitch it for a Story' method. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: By sewing different types of thick and thin threads onto a soft fabric base, I can create raised, bumpy lines that add a tactile texture.

questions.question_text: What is the main benefit of the 'View and Review' process after finishing a drawing? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Reviewing allows artists to get helpful feedback from others, understand different perspectives, and discover new ways to improve their future creative projects.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are designing an 'Imaginary Being' that lives deep in the ocean. Describe its physical features and the colors you would use. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: My imaginary sea creature has the glowing green body of a jellyfish and the silver tail of a dolphin. It possesses three large purple eyes to see in the dark water and has long, shimmering golden fins that sparkle like stars.

questions.question_text: Imagine you and your 'Time Team' are tasked with painting a large mural titled 'The Magic Forest'. Describe the process of working together. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: First, we would sketch the giant trees and mythical animals together on the wall. Next, we divide the tasks, with some friends painting the dark green leaves while others mix bright colors for the flowers, ensuring everyone contributes equally to the masterpiece.

questions.question_text: Explain how you would plan and draw a three-panel storyboard for 'Picturing Stories' about a bird building a nest. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: In the first panel, I would draw the bird flying with a small twig in its beak. In the second panel, the bird would be shown carefully weaving the twig into a half-built nest on a tree branch. Finally, the third panel would show the bird sitting proudly inside the completed, cozy nest.

questions.question_text: How would you design a poster titled 'Create a Scene' for a school play, ensuring the audience knows the time and place? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would draw a large, dramatic illustration of the play's main characters in the center using bright, eye-catching colors. Below the artwork, I would use bold, block letters to clearly write the date, time, and the school auditorium's name so that everyone can easily read the event details from a distance.
